job.title: Quant Trader, Basis Trading Desk
job.profile: 2-4 years at a prop shop, market maker, broker desk or crypto-native firm; strong production Python; working understanding of perps, funding, basis, margin and liquidation; real risk discipline; calm, clear communicator; willing to learn Rust. Hybrid trader-developer building execution analytics, reconciliation, reporting and automation.

anchors.0: No trading-desk experience: unrelated roles only, or a student with no trading work.
anchors.1: Under about two years, or only adjacent to a desk: internship, trading operations or settlements, research support, personal or retail trading, exchange or fintech engineering without a trading seat.
anchors.2: About 2-4 years in a trading or quant role at a prop shop, market maker, broker desk or crypto-native firm, with the role and dates stated.
anchors.3: As 2, plus clear ownership: named strategies, PnL or book responsibility, or desk workflows owned end to end (for example ran the basis or funding book, owned execution for a venue).

anchors.1: Python only in notebooks, coursework or ad-hoc scripts, or listed as a skill with no production use described.
anchors.2: Python running in production with concrete detail: a named service, pipeline or library, with tests, deployment, scheduling or monitoring mentioned.
anchors.3: As 2, plus ownership of production Python systems: testing or CI, packaging, monitoring or on-call, reviewing others' code, performance work, or systems others depend on daily.

criteria.name: Derivatives mechanics (perps, funding, basis, margin, liquidation)

anchors.1: Generic mentions only ('crypto trading', 'futures', 'derivatives', 'DeFi') with no mechanics.
anchors.2: Working understanding shown through specific work: funding-rate tracking or capture, basis calculation or cash-and-carry, margin monitoring, liquidation-price handling, mark versus index price, cross-margin behaviour.
anchors.3: Deep: designed or ran systems for funding or basis capture, margin optimisation across venues, liquidation modelling, or explains the mechanics quantitatively (annualised basis, funding settlement cadence, maintenance-margin ladders).

anchors.2: Concrete practice: position or exposure limits, kill switches, pre-trade checks, drawdown limits, monitoring and alerts, incident handling or post-mortems.
anchors.3: Owned the risk framework: designed limits and controls, reconciliation checks, incident response with measurable outcomes (losses avoided, zero limit breaches), or risk reporting used by others.

criteria.name: Tooling built and run in production (execution analytics, reconciliation, reporting, automation)

anchors.1: Ad-hoc scripts, spreadsheets or dashboards for own use.
anchors.2: Built tooling used by a desk or team in production: reconciliation, reporting, execution analytics (fills, slippage, TCA) or automation of a daily process.
anchors.3: Built and operated several production tools with ownership, users beyond self, reliability practices and measurable impact.

anchors.1: Learning Rust, or some C++ or Rust exposure (coursework, side project), or stated willingness to learn backed by some evidence.
anchors.2: Shipped Rust or C++ code, or meaningful latency engineering (profiling, async I/O, lock-free structures) in any setting.
anchors.3: Production Rust or C++ in trading systems (order gateways, market-data handlers, matching) with latency figures.

tier_rule.description: Deterministic. Scores are 0-3; a null (unknown, no evidence) counts as 0 here and is reported separately. total = sum of all six scores. core = trading_experience, python, derivatives. Rules are checked in order.

rules.when: any core criterion == 0 (including unknown), OR total <= 6
every core criterion >= 2 AND risk >= 2 AND total >= 12
